Liam: Heads-up — I'll be in SF Mon/Tue and Vancouver Wed-Fri for a 6-week client sprint starting May 4. Do we need a homebase change? How does the WFH stipend get prorated? Any tax/nexus risk I should flag?

Sofia (People Ops): Hey @Liam — quick answers: 1) No permanent homebase change for temporary stints under ~90 days; 2) Stipend is pro-rated by days in-location; 3) Payroll will confirm withholding rules for Canada/BC. Please submit dates and confirm you'll stay on Redwood payroll. :)

Liam: Dates: 2026-05-04 -> 2026-06-12 (6 weeks). I'll stay on Redwood payroll. Client office in Vancouver — does that change anything for the stipend?

Marco (Payroll): For Canada short trips we usually don't change homebase if it's under cumulative 60 days/year, but provinces have quirks. If payroll stays US-based we may still need to withhold/track for CPP/EI if any local tax authority considers work performed there. Can you fill the remote request form so I can run the withholding simulation? <https://hr.redwood.example/forms/remote-request>

Priya: Filing checklist: 1) Remote Work Notification in Confluence + dates; 2) Tag @Marco for payroll review; 3) Travel/stipend notes (client site vs personal WFH). Stipend formula we use: `stipend_amount * (days_in_location / days_in_month)`.

Sofia (People Ops): Example pro-rate calc for clarity: if monthly stipend = $200 and in Vancouver 3 out of 31 days in May -> Vancouver portion = 200 * 3/31 = $19.35 (we round to nearest dollar on payroll). We handle currency conversion and show it on your Pay Statement.

people-ops-bot: remote-request submitted by Liam — request ID RR-2026-451. Status: pending payroll review.

Liam: Thanks — also curious about benefits/health coverage while in Canada for short trips. Any exposure?

Priya: Your US benefits remain in effect for short trips. No plan changes for visits under ~90 days. If you extend beyond ~3 months or enroll dependents in Canada, we re-evaluate. Keep receipts for any medical expenses and mark them as "temporary travel" if you need to submit claims.

Marco (Payroll): One more ask: please confirm weekly split pattern (e.g., Mon/Tue SF, Wed-Fri YVR) per calendar week so I can test multi-jurisdiction rules. If your travel spikes over multiple employees in same client/region, that can create a tax nexus flag and we'd need leadership sign-off.

Liam: Will add the week-by-week schedule to the form today. Quick Q: is there an annual limit on number of short stints?

Sofia (People Ops): No hard cap for occasional stints. Operational rule: >6 months cumulative in a rolling 12-month window triggers a homebase review and possible payroll/legal change. :thumbsup:

Liam: Form submitted and schedule added. RR-2026-451. Thanks everyone!
